title: Build Your Project Folder
description: Set up an organised folder for a game idea, write notes, and move a file into the right place.

tasks.title: Files and Folders
tasks.explainer:
## Files Hold Work, Folders Organise Work

A **file** stores a piece of work. For example, `game-ideas.txt` can hold your written ideas.

A **folder** organises files and other folders. For example, a `Pictures` folder can hold image files.

Clear names make your work easier to find later.

A **path** is the route to an item:

```text
/Game Project/Notes/game-ideas.txt
```

To follow this path, open `Game Project`, then `Notes`, then `game-ideas.txt`.

tasks.title: File or Folder?
tasks.explainer: Match each item to the correct type.

subtasks.title: Create Your Project - 1
subtasks.explainer:
## Create a Project Folder

Create a folder called **Game Project** in the root folder. This will keep all of your game work together.
hints: Create a folder to keep all of your game work together.
Work in the root folder and choose the new-folder action.

subtasks.title: Create Your Project - 2
subtasks.explainer:
## Add an Ideas File

Inside `Game Project`, create a text file called `game-ideas.txt`.

The `.txt` ending is a **file extension**. It tells you that this is a plain text file.

subtasks.title: Create Your Project - 3
subtasks.explainer:
## Write Your Game Idea

Open `game-ideas.txt` and write one sentence about a maze game. Your sentence must include the word **maze**.

/Game Project/game-ideas.txt.content: My maze game will have a hidden treasure.

hints: Open the text file so you can edit its contents.
Write your own sentence about a game.
Make sure your sentence includes the word `maze`.

subtasks.title: Create Your Project - 4
subtasks.explainer:
## Add a Notes Folder

Inside `Game Project`, create a folder called **Notes**.

A folder stored inside another folder is sometimes called a **nested folder**.

/Game Project/game-ideas.txt.content: My maze game will have a hidden treasure.

hints: Create a new folder inside it.

tasks.title: Moving a File
tasks.explainer:
## Move Work with Cut and Paste

Your ideas file is useful, but it now belongs inside `Notes`.

- **Cut** selects an item to move.
- **Paste** places it in a new location.
- After a successful move, the file should no longer remain in its old location.

Cutting is not the same as deleting. The file and its contents are still available after you paste it.

tasks.title: Predict the Move
tasks.explainer: You cut `game-ideas.txt` from `Game Project` and paste it into `Notes`. Where should the file be afterwards?

options.feedback: That would describe copying. Cut and paste moves the original item.

options.text: Nowhere, because cutting always deletes a file
options.feedback: Cut prepares an item to move. Pasting places it in the new location.

tasks.title: Move the Ideas File
tasks.explainer:
## Put the File in the Right Place

Cut `/Game Project/game-ideas.txt` and paste it into `/Game Project/Notes/`.

Check that the file has moved and that your maze idea is still inside it.

/Game Project/Notes/game-ideas.txt.content: My maze game will have a hidden treasure.

hints: Open the `Notes` folder, then choose paste.
The old path `/Game Project/game-ideas.txt` should disappear.

tasks.title: Add a Design Folder
tasks.explainer:
## Independent Challenge

Inside `Game Project`, create a folder called `Designs`. Inside `Designs`, create a text file called `character.txt`.

/Game Project/Notes/game-ideas.txt.content: My maze game will have a hidden treasure.

hints: Create one new folder and one new text file.
The new folder belongs inside `Game Project`.

tasks.title: Finish the Sentence
tasks.text: A ___ stores a piece of work. A ___ organises items. Cut and paste will ___ an item.
